purpose: Maps prerequisite concepts and multi-step cognitive scaffolds across PH04 subtopics.

PH04-W01.title: Multi-force work-energy ledger with opposing friction and motor pull
PH04-W01.teaching: The work-energy theorem states that net work equals the algebraic sum of work done by every force acting on the body: W_net = sum(W_i) = Delta K. A force along displacement does positive work (+F*d), opposing friction does negative work (-f*d), and normal forces perpendicular to motion do zero work.
PH04-W01.worked: A 2 kg crate slides 3 m right under 10 N pull right and 4 N friction left. W_pull = +30 J, W_fric = -12 J, W_net = +18 J. With K_i = 1 J, K_f = 19 J ==> v_f = sqrt(19) ≈ 4.36 m/s.

PH04-W02.title: Piecewise spring contact and decoupled friction slide
PH04-W02.teaching: An unattached spring pushes a cart only while compressed (x > 0). At natural length (x = 0), contact ends and the spring exerts zero further force. Subsequent motion across a rough surface is governed solely by friction work W = -f*d.
PH04-W02.worked: A 2 kg cart released by an unattached spring (k = 200 N/m, x = 0.10 m) enters a 0.5 m rough strip with 1 N friction. U_s = 1.0 J. Friction work W_fric = -0.50 J. K_f = 0.50 J ==> v_f = sqrt(0.50) ≈ 0.707 m/s.
PH04-W02.check: Boundary continuity: velocity at spring release equals velocity entering the rough strip.

PH04-W03.title: Constant power non-linear velocity evolution and decaying acceleration
PH04-W03.teaching: Constant mechanical power P adds equal kinetic energy increments each second: K(t) = K_0 + P*t. Because K = 0.5*m*v^2, velocity grows as v(t) = sqrt(2*(K_0 + P*t)/m) (sub-linear), while driving force F = P/v and acceleration a = P/(m*v) decay over time. Acceleration is never constant under constant power.

PH04-W04.title: Distributed mass chain lifting work and center-of-mass depth
PH04-W04.teaching: For a uniform hanging chain of length x and linear mass density lambda = M/L, its mass is lambda*x and its center of mass is located at depth x/2. Its gravitational potential energy is U(x) = -0.5*lambda*g*x^2. Work required against gravity to pull hanging length from x_1 to x_2 is W = U(x_2) - U(x_1) = 0.5*lambda*g*(x_1^2 - x_2^2).
PH04-W04.worked: An 8 m rope of 4 kg (lambda = 0.5 kg/m) with 4 m hanging (U_1 = -40 J) is pulled until 2 m hangs (U_2 = -10 J). W = -10 - (-40) = +30 J.
PH04-W04.check: Quadratic dependence: lifting the upper half of hanging chain requires 3 times more work than the lower half.

PH04-W05.title: Graphical calculus selection: area versus slope from axis dimensions
PH04-W05.teaching: Graph calculus operations are determined strictly by coordinate axis units: Area on [F_x vs x] has units N*m = J, representing work W. Slope on [U vs x] has units J/m = N; by definition conservative force is F_x = -dU/dx. Slope on [s vs t] has units m/s, representing velocity v = ds/dt.
PH04-W05.worked: Card R (F_x vs x): triangle from (0,0) to (4 m, 8 N) has area W = 0.5*4*8 = 16 J. Card S (U vs x): slope = (8-2)/2 = +3 N ==> F_x = -3 N. Card T (s vs t): slope between (2 s, 4 m) and (5 s, 16 m) is v = (16-4)/(5-2) = 4 m/s.
PH04-W05.check: Dimensional homogeneity: Area units = y-unit * x-unit; Slope units = y-unit / x-unit.
